title: Cap. VIII Arg.: no just judge intends punitive justice per se — therefore God reprobates from foresight of demerit
pass_a_gloss: No just judge intends punitive justice of himself, but only upon the supposition of punishable fault: But in reprobating God intends to exercise his punitive and vindicative justice: Therefore he reprobates from foresight of the evil and demeritorious use of free will.
pass_b_english: They press further: a just judge never aims at punitive justice for its own sake — only once punishable fault is supposed. Yet God, they say, in the act of reprobating means to exercise punitive and vindicative justice. Hence reprobation must spring from foresight of free will's evil, demeritorious use.
source_text: Nullus justus judex per se intendit justitiam punitivam, sed tantum ex suppositione punibilis culpae: Sed in reprobando Deus intendit justitiam suam punitivam et vindicativam exercere: Ergo reprobat ex praescientia mali et demeritorii usus liberi arbitrii.
